questions.question:
Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of an algorithm?
a. Finiteness
b. Definiteness
c. Ambiguity
d. Input
questions.explanation: An algorithm must be finite, definite, effective and produce output from valid input. Ambiguity is the opposite of definiteness, because a step whose meaning is unclear cannot be executed reliably.

questions.question:
What does the term 'multiplicity' refer to in the context of a multiset?
a. Number of elements in the multiset
b. Number of unique elements in the multiset
c. Number of times an element appears in the multiset
d. Total number of multisets that can be formed from a given set

options.A: Number of elements in the multiset
options.B: Number of unique elements in the multiset
options.C: Number of times an element appears in the multiset
options.D: Total number of multisets that can be formed from a given set

questions.explanation: Multiplicity counts how many copies of a value a multiset holds, so {a, a, b} has multiplicity 2 for a. An ordinary set allows only one copy of each element.

questions.question:
Which approach is more suitable for problems with overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure?
a. Divide and Conquer
b. Dynamic Programming
c. Both a and b
d. Neither
questions.explanation: Dynamic programming suits problems whose subproblems repeat and whose global optimum is built from optimal sub-solutions, because each result is stored and reused. Divide and conquer assumes the subproblems are independent.

questions.question:
Which algorithm follows the Divide and Conquer approach?
a. Bubble Sort
b. Merge Sort
c. Selection Sort
d. Heap Sort
questions.explanation: Merge sort splits the array into halves, sorts each recursively and merges the results — the classic divide-and-conquer pattern. Bubble, selection and heap sort work on the array as a whole.

questions.question:
LIFO scheme is used in ________ data structure.
a) stack
b) queue
c) linked list
d) tree
questions.explanation: A stack pushes and pops at the same end, so the last item in is the first out (LIFO). A queue removes the oldest item first instead.

questions.question:
O-notation provides an asymptotic ________.
a) upper bound
b) lower bound
c) light bound
d) tight bound
questions.explanation: Big-O bounds a function from above, describing how the running time grows in the worst case. Omega gives a lower bound and Theta a tight bound on both sides.

questions.question:
ADT full form -
a) About Data Type
b) Abandoned Data Type
c) Abstract Data Type
d) Absolute Data Transaction
questions.explanation: ADT stands for Abstract Data Type: a type defined by the operations it supports and their behaviour, hiding the implementation. Stack and queue are standard examples.

questions.question:
In a multiset, elements are arranged in an unordered manner, with elements having a multiplicity of ________?
a) One
b) More than one
c) Zero
d) All of the above
questions.explanation: A multiset allows repeated members, so an element may occur zero, once or many times; any multiplicity is valid. A set restricts each element to a single occurrence.

questions.question:
Which of the following is/are property/properties of a dynamic programming problem?
a) Optimal substructure
b) Overlapping sub-problems
c) Greedy approach
d) Both optimal substructure and overlapping sub-problems

options.D: Both optimal substructure and overlapping sub-problems

questions.explanation: DP needs optimal substructure, so the best overall answer comes from best sub-answers, and overlapping subproblems, so the same subproblem recurs. Greedy is a different strategy.

questions.question:
Time complexity depends on -
a) Compile time
b) Run time
c) both Compile time and Run time
d) None of these

options.C: both Compile time and Run time

questions.explanation: Time complexity counts basic operations as a function of input size when the algorithm executes, so it is a run-time measure. Compile time belongs to the translator, not the algorithm.

questions.question:
The main measures of the efficiency of an algorithm are?
a) Time and space complexity
b) Data and space
c) Processor and memory
d) Complexity and capacity
questions.explanation: Efficiency is judged on two axes: time complexity, how the operation count grows, and space complexity, how memory use grows. Processor and data are not measures of the algorithm itself.

questions.question:
If A = {x, y, z}, number of elements of the power set of A is:
a) 6
b) 8
c) 10
d) 12
questions.explanation: A power set holds every subset, and each of the n elements is either included or not, giving 2^n subsets. For three elements that is 2³ = 8.
Sets are equal when they contain exactly the same members, because order and repetition do not matter. {5,6,8,9} and {6,8,5,9} contain the same four numbers.

questions.question:
Which of the following is asymptotically smallest?
a) n
b) log n
c) n log n
d) 2n
questions.explanation: log n grows more slowly than n, n log n or 2n, so it is asymptotically the smallest here. That is why binary search beats a linear scan on large inputs.

questions.question:
Name of the data structure used by recursion is:
a) Stack
b) Queue
c) Array
d) Linked list
questions.explanation: Each recursive call saves its parameters and return address on the run-time stack, and each return pops them. That LIFO behaviour is why recursion is said to use a stack.

questions.question:
Big O notation derives the ________ case.
a) Best
b) Average
c) Worst
d) All cases
questions.explanation: Big-O gives an upper bound, so it describes the worst case: the maximum time the algorithm can take for an input of size n. Best case is expressed with Omega.

questions.question:
________ notation gives the lower bound of the function f(n).
a) Big-O
b) Theta
c) Omega
d) None
questions.explanation: Omega (Ω) bounds the function from below, so it captures the minimum work or best case. Big-O is the upper bound and Theta the tight two-sided bound.

Theta (Θ) notation provides which type of bound for a function?
a) Upper bound only
b) Lower bound only
c) Both upper and lower bound (tight bound)
d) No bound

options.C: Both upper and lower bound (tight bound)

questions.explanation: Theta (Θ) means the growth rate is bounded both above and below by the same function, so it is a tight bound. Big-O alone gives only the upper side.

questions.question:
Which of the following best defines space complexity?
a) Time taken by an algorithm to execute
b) Amount of memory used by an algorithm as a function of input size
c) Number of operations performed
d) Size of the input data

options.A: Time taken by an algorithm to execute
options.B: Amount of memory used by an algorithm as a function of input size

questions.explanation: Space complexity is the total memory an algorithm needs, including auxiliary arrays and the run-time stack, as a function of input size. The size of the input alone is not the measure.
